cases.purpose: On a 20x70 PTY with LINES and COLUMNS unset, tput lines and tput cols written to the terminal report 20 and 70.
cases.script:
unset LINES COLUMNS
printf 'L='; tput lines; printf 'C='; tput cols; printf 'S-DONE\n'
cases.oracle: ncurses-bin 6.5 tput(1) on the reference PATH (TIOCGWINSZ for lines/cols when LINES/COLUMNS are unset; init/reset strings and reset's sane termios; compiled terminfo via TERMINFO, TERMINFO_DIRS, ~/.terminfo; padding per baud rate); screen effects decoded independently by pyte.
cases.comparison: parity: reference must show the window size; raw PTY regex

cases.purpose: After the PTY is resized from 20x70 to 30x100, a new tput lines/cols query reports 30 and 100.
cases.script:
unset LINES COLUMNS
printf 'R0\n'; IFS= read -r _
printf 'L='; tput lines; printf 'C='; tput cols; printf 'R-DONE\n'
cases.oracle: ncurses-bin 6.5 tput(1) on the reference PATH (TIOCGWINSZ for lines/cols when LINES/COLUMNS are unset; init/reset strings and reset's sane termios; compiled terminfo via TERMINFO, TERMINFO_DIRS, ~/.terminfo; padding per baud rate); screen effects decoded independently by pyte.
cases.comparison: parity: reference must show the new size; raw PTY regex

cases.purpose: Visible effect of emitted strings: text written before tput clear is gone; after tput cup 5 10, X lands at (5,10); tput bold makes the following B bold and tput sgr0 makes N plain.
cases.script:
printf 'junk-before-clear'; tput clear; tput cup 5 10; printf X; tput bold; printf B; tput sgr0; printf N
tput cup 8 0; printf END
cases.oracle: ncurses-bin 6.5 tput(1) on the reference PATH (TIOCGWINSZ for lines/cols when LINES/COLUMNS are unset; init/reset strings and reset's sane termios; compiled terminfo via TERMINFO, TERMINFO_DIRS, ~/.terminfo; padding per baud rate); screen effects decoded independently by pyte.
cases.comparison: parity with semantic screen assertions (pyte rows, cursor and cells) satisfied by the reference first

cases.purpose: With echo, icanon and onlcr turned off, tput reset emits the reset strings and restores sane terminal-driver modes (echo, icanon, onlcr on); raw output bytes are compared and the original modes restored afterwards.
cases.script:
s=$(/usr/bin/stty -g)
/usr/bin/stty -echo -icanon -onlcr
tput reset; echo "rc=$?" > rc
/usr/bin/python3 modes.py > modes-after
printf 'X-DONE\n'
/usr/bin/stty "$s"
cases.oracle: ncurses-bin 6.5 tput(1) on the reference PATH (TIOCGWINSZ for lines/cols when LINES/COLUMNS are unset; init/reset strings and reset's sane termios; compiled terminfo via TERMINFO, TERMINFO_DIRS, ~/.terminfo; padding per baud rate); screen effects decoded independently by pyte.
cases.comparison: parity: reference must restore the modes (modes-after exact); byte parity of the raw PTY output (compare_screen)

files.modes.py:
import termios
a = termios.tcgetattr(0)
print('echo=%d icanon=%d onlcr=%d' % (bool(a[3] & termios.ECHO), bool(a[3] & termios.ICANON), bool(a[1] & termios.ONLCR)))

cases.purpose: tput init and tput reset with no terminal on stdin, stdout or stderr (all files or pipes): status, stdout and stderr bytes match ncurses.
cases.script:
tput init < /dev/null > init-out 2> init-err; echo "init=$?" > rc
tput reset < /dev/null > reset-out 2> reset-err; echo "reset=$?" >> rc
cases.oracle: ncurses-bin 6.5 tput(1) on the reference PATH (TIOCGWINSZ for lines/cols when LINES/COLUMNS are unset; init/reset strings and reset's sane termios; compiled terminfo via TERMINFO, TERMINFO_DIRS, ~/.terminfo; padding per baud rate); screen effects decoded independently by pyte.
cases.comparison: byte parity vs ncurses tput of status lines and captured output files

cases.purpose: Capabilities from compiled terminfo built by trusted tic in setup: an entry in $TERMINFO (string, parameterized cup, alias name, extended Xfx capability), a user vt100 entry overriding the system one, the same entry through TERMINFO_DIRS, an entry in ~/.terminfo, and the system vt100 entry once TERMINFO is unset.
cases.script:
export TERMINFO=$PWD/ti
tput -T fx215 bold > r1-bold; echo "bold=$?" > rc
tput -T fx215 cup 3 4 > r1-cup; echo "cup=$?" >> rc
tput -T fixture-alias bold > r3-alias; echo "alias=$?" >> rc
tput -T fx215 Xfx > r4-ext; echo "ext=$?" >> rc
tput -T vt100 bold > r2-override; echo "override=$?" >> rc
unset TERMINFO
TERMINFO_DIRS=$PWD/ti tput -T fx215 sgr0 > r1-dirs; echo "dirs=$?" >> rc
tput -T fxhome bold > r1-home; echo "home=$?" >> rc
tput -T vt100 bold > system-vt100-bold; echo "system=$?" >> rc
cases.oracle: ncurses-bin 6.5 tput(1) on the reference PATH (TIOCGWINSZ for lines/cols when LINES/COLUMNS are unset; init/reset strings and reset's sane termios; compiled terminfo via TERMINFO, TERMINFO_DIRS, ~/.terminfo; padding per baud rate); screen effects decoded independently by pyte.
cases.comparison: byte parity vs ncurses tput; exact expectations for the fixture entries (the system vt100 bold bytes are compared by parity only)
cases.setup_script:
mkdir -p ti "$HOME/.terminfo"
tic -x -o "$PWD/ti" fx.src
tic -x -o "$HOME/.terminfo" home.src

files.fx.src:
fx215|fixture-alias|worker 215 fixture terminal,
	am, cols#123, lines#45,
	bold=BOLD215, clear=CLR215, cup=CUP%p1%d;%p2%dX, sgr0=SGR0215,
	Xfx=XFX215,
vt100|fixture override of the system vt100 entry,
	bold=OVERRIDE-BOLD, cols#80, lines#24,
fxpad|fixture with mandatory padding,
	cols#80, lines#24, clear=CLR$<10/>,

expected_files.rc:
bold=0
cup=0
alias=0
ext=0
override=0
dirs=0
home=0
system=0
